Subject: ACME POC - Integration planning & success criteria

Hi John / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on objectives. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the 2-week POC so we can get engineering unblocked: 

Summary / goals
- Primary success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 300ms for user-facing generation flows; throughput target ~50 RPS for our sandbox traffic; qualitative accuracy: >85% human pass rate on the provided evaluation set.
- Data constraints: customer data stays in US region, no persistent storage of ACME PII outside their environment (we discussed redaction).

Integration scope (MVP)
- Integrate Redwood SDK to call text-generation and streaming endpoints.
- Validate streaming + tool-calling for retrieval-augmented workflows (RAG).
- Measure latency, tokens/cost, and implement prefix caching for hot prompts.

Owners / timeline
- Redwood: Dev Patel (integration lead), Rishi Malhotra (SE support)
- ACME: Anil Kapoor (eng lead), Priya Reddy (product)
- Proposed kickoff: Wed June 30, integration window: ~2 weeks (Jun 30 - Jul 14)

Requests for ACME
- Provide representative sample payloads and eval prompt set (anonymized).
- Service account or API key for sandbox environment + test dataset link.

Attachments: redwood-poc-mvp-plan.pdf (high-level plan + checklist)

Next steps
1) Please confirm success criteria above or flag additions.
2) ACME to share sample payloads and preferred kickoff time — we can do Wed 6/30 morning PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the recap. That aligns well with our internal goals. A few clarifications from our side: 

Success criteria tweaks
- Latency: target 95p < 300ms for short-form generation (<= 256 tokens). For longer generation (>1k tokens) we expect slower but want stable throughput.
- Quality: we'll run a 100-example blind eval (provided) and expect >85% pass as you noted.
- Cost: we'll track tokens/unit cost, but this won't block POC acceptance.

Technical / infra notes
- We require the sandbox to be in us-east-1 and to restrict egress to our testing VPC.
- We can provide sample prompts + 1k anonymized records (see attached).

Timeline / people
- Anil Kapoor (eng lead) will own the integration on our side — cc'd.
- Wed 6/30 morning PT works for a 60-min kickoff. Priya can join.

Attaching: acme-poc-requirements.xlsx with sample payloads and dataset schema.

John
Senior Product Manager | Acme Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: ACME POC - Integration planning & success criteria

John / team — thanks for the file. A few technical notes to prepare for the kickoff and to accelerate integration: 

1) SDK + API routes - We recommend starting with our Node/Python SDK for quick integration. Typical flow:
   - POST /v1/sessions to create a session for streaming use-cases
   - PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/stream to open a streaming response (WS / HTTP chunked)
   - POST /v1/generate for synchronous generation (non-stream).
   - POST /v1/tools/invoke for tool-calling hooks (RAG retrieval or DB lookups).

2) Streaming best practices - Use small initial chunk sizes for interactive flows, enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts to reduce cold-token time. We'll demo with websocket streaming in the kickoff.

3) Auth & sandbox
- Please provide a service account key for a sandbox account scoped to us-east-1. For the POC we can restrict outbound egress to ACME IPs.

4) Metrics & SLOs
- We'll ship a lightweight dashboard (token usage, 95p latency, error rate) and provide a perf report at the end of week 1 and week 2.

5) Next actions for kickoff
   - ACME: upload sample payloads and test dataset link (John/Anil)
   - Redwood: Dev to prepare SDK example repo and Postman collection

I'm assigning Dev Patel as integration owner on our side (cc). Dev, can you confirm the SDK repo and an approximate ETA for the demo artifacts?

Thanks,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
